newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran minister to probe attack in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Iran minister to probe attack in Pakistan.

text.p: Iran's deputy foreign minister will lead a delegation to Pakistan this weekend to investigate a recent attack on an Iranian cultural centre in which eight people were killed, Iran's news agency IRNA said on Wednesday.
"Morteza Sarmadi will arrive in Islamabad on Saturday, March 1, to investigate the terrorist attack on the Iranian cultural centre in the city of Multan," the official agency said.
Sarmadi would also discuss the incident in the central Punjab province with top Pakistani officials, IRNA said.
The Multan attack on February 20 was the second on an Iranian cultural centre in Pakistan in a month.
"Iran has...urged Pakistan to be more cautious in the protection of its diplomatic missions," IRNA said.
A statement issued by the Iranian consulate-general in the Punjab capital Lahore blamed unspecified "anti-Islamic agents of world imperialism" for the February attack.

On January 19, a crowd of Sunni Moslem militants ransacked and burned the Iranian cultural centre in Lahore a day after a bomb blast there killed the leader of the militant Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP) group.
SSP followers blamed Shi'ite militants for the Lahore bombing, which killed 26 people and wounded about 90. Shi'ite groups denied they were involved.
IRNA quoted news reports on Wednesday as saying Pakistan had arrested seven people in connection with the Multan attack.
